question: A circle that has a diameter of 10 centimeters... A line is tangent to the circle. What is the angle between the tangent and the diameter at the point of contact?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

By the fundamental properties of circles, the radius drawn to the point of tangency is always perpendicular to the tangent line.

Since the diameter is a straight line that contains the radius, it is also perpendicular to the tangent at the point of contact.

The length of the diameter (10 cm) is given only to distract from this universal geometric truth.

**∴ The correct answer is 90°.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Diameter of the circle = 10 cm

A straight line is tangent to the circle.
